PullRequest.Title: Implement experimental mode and permissions picker integration
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request implements a new experimental mode and permissions picker for the agent host, inspired by the recent model picker design. Key changes include:

- **Picker Structure**: The permissions picker is now integrated below the mode picker, with a flyout that opens directly above the selected label.
- **Visual Design**: The mode label is the primary focus, with quieter, colored permission text. The permissions flyout is styled to match the main picker.
- **Iconography**: A compact icon is used for the mode picker, and a gear icon has been added to access permission settings.
- **Hover Behavior**: Individual hover affordances have been removed for a cleaner look, with a shared hover treatment for the entire control.
- **Accessibility**: Keyboard navigation and focus behaviors have been refined to ensure smooth transitions between the mode and permissions menus.

The changes are gated behind the `chat.experimentalModePermissionsPicker` setting and are currently limited to the Copilot agent host. All modifications have been verified with extensive testing, ensuring functionality across different themes and environments.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and reactively refresh the combined Mode/Permissions control in an Agent Host composer or Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session/config observables synchronously recompute eligibility and presentation, then rebuild or refresh the two-button trigger before the toolbar reflects the new state.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One mode control per active composer surface, plus the pre-existing separate permission control instance; updates scale with session/config changes and the small static schema.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable reactions run synchronously and serially. Popup visibility is coalesced by the shared ActionWidgetService, and trigger listener stores are disposed before replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved session configuration and provisional configuration are reused through the existing subscription/overlay state. The new presentation reads those in-memory values and adds no cache or miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the render and disposal paths are explicit, and the new permission delegate only performs in-memory provider/configuration lookups.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact DOM/layout duration depends on theme and host surface, but the changed work is bounded to two buttons and a handful of labels/listeners per config update.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR adds bounded synchronous DOM work and one extra provider/config observer, but no hot-loop, unbounded retention, or expensive boundary on this path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and navigate the combined picker for static Copilot Agent Host mode and permission schemas
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A click builds mode and permission action arrays, creates one ActionListWidget, lays it out, and focuses the requested group before interaction can continue.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective list is the static mode enum plus three permission levels, optional sandbox/learn-more rows, headers, and separators; tests establish roughly 13 total rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mode and permission item construction is awaited sequentially, but combined mode explicitly rejects enumDynamic schemas, so both operations are synchronous in-memory enumeration. Only one popup can be visible.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current resolved schema/value is read from existing subscription or provisional state. No cold network/IPC fetch occurs for a combined picker and reopening reconstructs only the small action list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: shouldCombineModeAndPermissions requires both schemas to be non-dynamic, and the item-building call path was traced through _getItems.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout cost varies by viewport, but the list is small and virtualized; useFullHeight changes only the cap, not item cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added list scans, focus-group restoration, and highlight updates are linear in a small fixed row count and do not cross an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or filter a non-combined editor Agent Host picker with a dynamic schema
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening requests session-config completions before showing the popup; subsequent filter text is passed through the existing Delayer before requesting refreshed completions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call on open for a dynamic property, plus coalesced filter calls; never two calls for the combined mode/permissions UI because dynamic schemas fail its gate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same picker already called sessionConfigCompletions for enumDynamic schemas on open and through its filter delegate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial call must finish before the popup is shown; filtered calls must finish before refreshed rows are applied.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One completion request for the selected property on open, then at most the delayer's effective request cadence for typed filter values.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing Delayer coalesces filter updates and ActionList cancellation discards superseded results. Combined mode is disabled for dynamic schemas, so the PR does not add a second permission completion request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no explicit completion cache; warm behavior remains the prior service behavior. Static schemas avoid this boundary entirely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only completion call is guarded by schema.enumDynamic, while combined eligibility requires !enumDynamic for both schemas.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Service latency depends on provider implementation, but call cardinality and gating are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff refactors property selection but does not increase completion-call count or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initialize Agent Host controls for an untitled chat session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing picker attachment path resolves initial session configuration and obtains or creates a provisional backend session so defaults are available before first send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve initial Agent Host session configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-picker initialization behavior; the PR does not add another picker instance or another call site.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each dedicated AgentHostChatInputPicker already resolved initial configuration during attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs asynchronously while the chip waits for resolved schema/defaults; first-send configuration can depend on the result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or retrieve a provisional backend session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Multiple chip requests are coalesced to one logical provisional per session resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same eager provisional getOrCreate path existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs asynchronously and supplies configuration used when the first message materializes the session.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical provisional session per chat resource, although multiple existing chip instances can race to request it.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The provisional service is documented and used as idempotent/serialized; each picker has a cancellable initial resolve tied to the current session resource.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _initialResolved caches the resolved result per resource, and the provisional service coalesces getOrCreate for the same resource. Session changes cancel stale resolves.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the unchanged initialization call path and its cancellation/coalescing ownership were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific resolve duration is unknown, but this PR neither increases picker count nor defeats coalescing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Expensive initialization is pre-existing and remains cached/coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use shared ActionList filtering, section expansion, focus-group navigation, and popup cleanup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Filtering and section changes rebuild the visible item array and splice the virtualized list; focus or hover updates at most the previous and current highlighted rows. Hiding clears submenu/widget disposables.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Generic filtering gains one scan of all menu items; focus-group cleanup can additionally scale with retained groups, but current production use introduced by this PR has two groups and a small list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Filtering cancellation prevents stale async filter results; UI updates are synchronous. Submenu timers are cancelled and disposables cleared on hide/replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Highlight state is retained only for groups in the current item set and stale entries are removed during list updates; no external cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added scans and lifecycle behavior; low prevalence/magnitude for any user-visible cost because effective production cardinality is bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Other future callers could supply larger group sets, but repository search found focusGroup production use only in this new small combined picker; theoretical quadratic behavior is not a realistic current trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The shared extra scan is dominated by existing filter/list reconstruction at current cardinalities, and cleanup ownership remains bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose Configure Permissions or Learn More from the combined picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The popup closes, then an explicit user action opens Settings with a fixed query or opens the existing documentation URL.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the Settings UI with the permissions query
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit Configure Permissions activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The combined picker and its inline Configure Permissions action did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It is the requested navigation and occurs after the popup closes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opener invocation per explicit Learn More activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The standalone permission picker already exposed the same documentation navigation; the PR reuses it inline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It is the requested action, not background or multiplied work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one boundary-like navigation per explicit activation; the fixed settings query has a constant number of setting IDs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selection closes the popup before awaiting navigation; repeated activation requires reopening the picker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is needed because work is explicit and single-shot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both action handlers and popup-close ordering are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Settings/editor startup cost varies, but it is intentional, explicit, and never automatic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. These boundaries are user-requested single-shot actions with constant cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 38 changed files. Traced render/layout work, action-list filtering and focus groups, observer/listener lifecycles, initial Agent Host resolution, dynamic completion IPC, popup concurrency, and settings/navigation actions. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
